goal: Implement Phase G Recommendation A only: add standardized, purely diagnostic per-phase and Phase-2 per-test timing observability to the existing canonical scripts/verify_assurance_baseline.py path. Preserve all existing assurance pass/fail semantics, discovery, ordering, mandatory coverage anchors, golden coverage, hosted CI command, promotion authority, short-circuit behavior, and the exact canonical terminal success string. This milestone does not authorize optimization, a separate fast runner, parallelism, sharding, caching/skipping, framework migration, slow-test exclusion, trace infrastructure, or Phase I work.
acceptance_conditions: Use Python standard-library monotonic timing via time.perf_counter or an equivalent monotonic high-resolution clock; no external dependency or platform-specific shell timing.
Each invoked canonical phase 0, 1, 2, and 3 emits exactly one standardized diagnostic phase-duration record using a stable machine-readable text grammar with a non-negative duration in seconds.
Each Phase 2 test that is actually executed emits exactly one standardized diagnostic per-test duration record naming the test filename and a non-negative duration in seconds, including failed tests.
Phase timing is emitted for an invoked phase even when that phase returns failure; later phases still do not execute after the first failed phase.
Timing output is diagnostic only and never participates in pass/fail, test discovery, ordering, mandatory-anchor validation, golden-case semantics, promotion authority, or success determination.
The exact terminal success string ALL PHASES PASSED: canonical assurance baseline verified. remains byte-for-byte unchanged and is emitted only when all four canonical phases succeed.
Phase 2 discovery remains tests/*_test.py in deterministic lexicographic filename order; all nine mandatory Phase 2 anchors remain unchanged.
Phase 3 continues to invoke golden-tests/run_job_analysis_golden_set.py through the existing canonical path with unchanged success/failure semantics.
No wall-clock threshold, performance SLA, optimization decision, or reliability inference is added; tests use deterministic/fake timing rather than asserting machine-dependent runtimes.
No path outside allowed_paths changes and no hosted workflow command changes.
Independent Cursor adversarial review of immutable frozen bytes returns SAFE before promotion.
